title: Safety evaluation for dual-use science
bottleneck: The same model that accelerates biology and chemistry research can accelerate bioweapon and chemical-weapon development, and we have no validated way to measure where the line is. Capability evaluations for uplift — how much a model helps a malicious actor — are nascent, contested, and easy to game; labs disagree on thresholds and evaluations lag the models. Under-measuring risks catastrophe; over-measuring blocks legitimate science.
why_it_blocks: This is the evaluation problem with the highest stakes: a wrong answer in either direction costs lives or cripples beneficial research.
current_state: Labs publish biosecurity evaluations of varying rigor; experts warn weak methods fuel misleading claims about safety. Labs publish safety evaluations for dual-use domains, but the refusal benchmarks are narrow and easily circumvented.
